paragraphs: Here's what I want you to hold onto, friend. Jonah ran the other way, and the LORD didn't leave him alone out there. Jonah says, "In my distress I called to the LORD, and He answered me." (Jonah 2:2) Think about that. Jonah was in the worst spot of his whole life, and the LORD still heard his voice.

Now look at WHEN Jonah's prayer turns. He says, "As my life was fading away, I remembered the LORD." (Jonah 2:7) He didn't wait until things got comfortable, and he didn't wait until he had the right words. He said it plain, from the bottom, and it went up to God's holy temple. Friend, I know a little about the bottom of things, and I'm telling you, that's a fine place to start talking to God.

Then Jonah ends with something worth repeating to a friend: "Salvation is from the LORD!" (Jonah 2:9) He says he will sacrifice with the voice of thanksgiving, and the LORD commands the fish and Jonah lands on dry land (Jonah 2:10). So when you feel like you've swum too far from where God asked you to be, remember this: you can call to Him and give thanks, because rescue is His work. The story isn't over for Jonah, and the same LORD who rescued him is still the One who saves.
